# Vendored Speedscope

Speedscope 1.25.0, commit `810efdf0a4868bb28f1300f4daacd0db6b8a95bd`, MIT. The bundled Source Code Pro font has its own included license. All viewer assets are served locally. Profile data never goes to the upstream service.

The `compact-labels.patch` shortens canvas and table labels and makes a single frame click zoom to that frame and its descendants. Dragging still pans. Frame identity, full-symbol tooltips, selected-frame inspection, search and exports remain unchanged. Search temporarily displays full labels so matching character ranges remain accurate. The toolbar calls the chronological view Sample Order because neither CPU weights nor sample counts represent wall-clock position. Tooltips show Self and Total weights, percentages, and actual retained sample counts. Weighted samples keep their counts through aggregation and caller/callee views. Recursion-flattened nodes omit counts when they cannot be reconstructed. Automatic WASM demangling is disabled because the backend already supplies bounded demangled names and retains raw symbols. This preserves canonical names and avoids weakening script CSP.

To reproduce, clone the pinned upstream commit, verify `package-lock.json` against `manifest.json`, apply the patch, run `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`, then `node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/build-release.ts --outdir dist/profile-viewer --protocol http`. The recorded build used Node 24.7.0 and npm 11.5.1. Copy non-map assets, upstream LICENSE and assets/source-code-pro/LICENSE.md. Regenerate manifest hashes and the explicit Rust asset match. No package installation or asset build runs in the deployed service.

Source maps are omitted. The profile exporter retains canonical symbols; shortened labels are never used to merge frames. Source links are not invented from symbol names.
